messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: 08:03 UTC — High error rate observed for outbound connections from eu-west-2a private subnets. Affected: NAT gateway gw-0a1b2c3d, route table rtb-09f8e7d6. Paging oncall.
oncall-ux: I'm on it. pinging infra and netops. any customer reports yet? :eyes:
alex: seeing TCP timeouts to external hosts from pods in eu-west-2a. 5xxs for customers hitting /api/generate with 504s. Metric graph: spike at 08:02.
maya: adding context — around 08:00 we pushed a terraform change that updated NACLs for a security cleanup. not sure if related.
raj: I'm seeing route table associate/replace events in cloudtrail with multiple rapid flips: user=infra-ci, source=automation. Could be a runaway job.
samir: ssh'd into a jump and ran `curl -v https://api.ipify.org` from a private instance — TCP handshake stalls after SYN-ACK. ARP looks fine. NAT gateway shows unhealthy in console.
leo: marking customer-impact: some EU customers seeing increased latency and errors. CS says 4 high-priority tickets opened.
oncall-ux: OK we need immediate mitigation. Rollback NACL change? Or detach NAT and reattach a fresh NAT in another AZ? Runbook suggests: if NAT gateway unhealthy, fail over to NAT instance.
alex: can we attach a standby NAT instance into the private subnets quickly? I have an AMI and userdata script ready. `deploy/nat-standby` runbook id: RB-112
maya: hold — I see automation repeatedly associating route table to subnet eu-west-2a-priv-01 then back to eu-west-2a-priv-02. Looks like a CI job looping on route propagation. I'm going to pause infra-automation.
raj: stopped infra-automation job (job id 8743). Confirmed hooks disabled. route churn slowed but NAT still unhealthy — might be NACL drop leftover.
samir: listing NACL rules for subnet-priv-01: `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0abcd`. Found an explicit DENY on ephemeral ports 32768-65535 for 0.0.0.0/0 added at 07:59.
leo: that DENY would break outbound ephemeral replies. Who applied that rule? check commit history.
maya: it was part of the terraform change — an overly broad deny. I already reverted the commit in the infra repo and applied a targeted rule. Pushing `terraform apply -target=aws_network_acl.rule-allow-ephemeral` now.
alex: while that applies, I'm booting the NAT instance and updating route table to point to instance id i-0f1e2d3c (temporary). Command: `aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-09f8e7d6 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --instance-id i-0f1e2d3c`
oncall-ux: customer-success, can you post an update to the affected customers? mention we're mitigating and rolling back a NACL rule ASAP.
customer-success: Posted to affected customers: "We are investigating connectivity issues impacting outbound traffic from EU region; mitigation in progress. No data loss. We'll update within 30 minutes." :white_check_mark:
raj: terraform apply completed, NACL DENY removed. Confirming `tcpdump` on a pod now shows SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK completing. connectivity looks better.
samir: NAT instance is up and route table updated. `curl -v https://api.ipify.org` returns IP 3.120.45.67 successfully. Starting smoke tests for /api/generate.
alex: smoke tests passing from eu-west-2a via NAT instance. Rolling back to NAT gateway once healthy? NAT gateway still shows status=Failed in cloud console.
maya: NAT gateway metrics show high error count around the time of NACL change. Shouldn't try to re-associate until GW health recovers. Let's keep NAT instance for now and monitor cost/throughput.
leo: timeline note for postmortem: root cause appears to be an overly broad NACL deny pushed by automation, compounded by a route table churn from a CI job that amplified impact. Immediate fix: remove DENY and attach NAT instance as stopgap.
oncall-ux: handing off to second on-call for follow-up and postmortem. @raj please take over rotations and follow-up actions.
raj: taking over. I'll collect CloudTrail, TF plan, and automation logs. Will file an incident report and link runbook steps.
customer-success: customers updated with mitigation complete and ETA for full remediation. Will keep them updated when NAT gateway is restored or replaced.
incident-bot: Incident severity updated to Sev2 at 08:31 UTC. Recording timeline and attendees.
raj: next actions: (1) verify no other subnets have same NACL deny, (2) audit infra-automation triggers, (3) schedule a canary rollback test for NACL changes in staging. Assigning tasks and tagging owners in issue.
alex: note — add a guard in CI to prevent NACL denies that block ephemeral port range. I'll draft a PR for a tf-lint rule.
maya: TL;DR for pager: remove broad NACL deny, pause automation, spin NAT instance, re-route traffic. Follow-up: CI guard + postmortem + customer comms.
leo: closing note — cost impact: NAT instance running ~2 hours. CS to reconcile credits for affected customers.
raj: thanks everyone. I'll post the incident report in #incidents/postmortems after analysis. End of thread.
